$comment: §22 Unlock Economy + §4 Population Scale & the Milestone Ladder of docs/METROPOLIS-MASTER-v2.1.md, authored into the 12 Development-Point progression trees §22 names verbatim (Roads, Electricity, Water & Gas, Health & Deathcare, Education, Fire, Police, Garbage, Parks & Rec, Transport, Communications, Welfare), each covering all 13 milestone tiers (1=Wilderness .. 13=Centopolis). FEAT-029 / data.unlocktrees. Every real node transcribes one §10 Service & Feature Inventory item — its specRef cites §10's literal wording (e.g. '§10: public transport (bus → rail → metro)') and, where §4's ladder gates it, the §4 tier — so nothing here is invented; every dpCost/prereqTier is a placeholder v1 shape, NOT a measured balance value. Node ids are stable lowercase slugs (buildingIDPattern) and are the lookup keys data.catalogue's unlock.dp field may reference (MOD-032 AC-10). See meta for the placeholder disclosure, the ASM-481 no-op-node convention, and the ASM-482 floor rule.

meta.placeholderDisclosure: Every dpCost and prereqTier in this file is a placeholder v1 shape, not a measured balance value: dpCost equals the node's milestone tier (1-13, a monotonic 'costs as many DP as its tier' placeholder) and prereqTier equals that same tier. No §22/§4 figure exists for DP costs or spend order — M2 Batch tuning territory, the same carve-out data.catalogue.md and data.modes-naming.md use.
meta.noopConvention: ASM-481 (lead-ACCEPTED): every category tree covers all 13 milestone tiers. Where §10 names no signature content for a category at a tier, the tier is represented by an explicit kind:'none' node whose note explains the absence — never by a silently absent tier, so an authoring gap and a deliberate no-op stay distinguishable.
meta.floorRule: ASM-482 (lead-ACCEPTED): every category carries at least 13 nodes (one per tier minimum — 12 categories x 13 tiers, derived from FEAT-029's own title, not an invented constant).
